adverse_media.summary: In Terna Energy Trading doo v Revolut Ltd [2024] EWHC 1419 (Comm), a Serbian energy trader claims EUR 700,000 that it paid into a fraudster's Revolut account in an invoice scam. The High Court refused Revolut Ltd's application for reverse summary judgment or strike-out, so the claim goes to trial. Revolut was later given permission to appeal.
adverse_media.status: Ongoing. Revolut has permission to appeal; no Court of Appeal judgment was found.

adverse_media.summary: The FCA, supported by the National Crime Agency, reportedly examined 'alleged process failings' after Revolut released up to GBP 1.7m from accounts the NCA had flagged as suspicious during summer 2023. The article does not name the Revolut legal entity, but the FCA-regulated UK firm at the time was Revolut Ltd.
adverse_media.status: Outcome not reported. No FCA final notice or penalty was found.

adverse_media.summary: BDO qualified its opinion on Revolut's 2021 accounts. It could not verify the 'completeness or occurrence' of about GBP 477m of GBP 636m revenue (about 75%) and warned that figures 'may be materially misstated', pointing to IT control weaknesses. The accounts were also filed late.
adverse_media.status: Historical. Revolut says the IT issue was fixed in 2021.

adverse_media.summary: The Telegraph reported that Revolut turned off a new sanctions screening system from July to September 2018 because it produced too many false positives, and that an internal investigation found the decision was wrong. Revolut said it went back to its earlier controls, reviewed all transactions and found no breaches. It did not notify the FCA. The CFO resigned around the same time, and Revolut said this was unrelated.

output.risk_rationale: Revolut Ltd (08804411; LEI 213800MQORWPL582SW82) is an active London company incorporated on 2013-12-06. Its records are clear and consistent between Companies House and GLEIF (GLEIF last updated 2026-10-26). It is 75% or more owned by Revolut Group Holdings Ltd (12743269), whose only registered PSC is CEO Nikolay Storonskiy, a British national holding 25-50%. No sanctions match was found for the entity, its parent or the UBO on OFAC, OFSI or EU lists, based on the OpenSanctions aggregator as of 2026-11-10; the official OFAC and UK search tools could not be queried directly. No director or owner was found to be a PEP. The rating is still medium rather than low for four reasons: (i) the UBO's reported father, a Gazprom Promgaz executive, has been on Ukraine's NSDC sanctions list since 2022-10-19, a connected-person risk although he has no role at Revolut Ltd; (ii) the 2023 FCA/NCA probe into money released from accounts flagged as suspicious, with no outcome published; (iii) the 2018 suspension of sanctions screening and BDO's qualified 2021 audit opinion over about 75% of revenue; (iv) continuing APP-fraud litigation (Terna, [2024] EWHC 1419) and heavy fraud-complaint volumes. Excluded from this entity's findings (namesakes_excluded = 8): 4 French AMF scam-domain warnings, the Slovenian firm 'REVOLUT - G d.o.o.', the Ukraine-sanctioned Nikolay M. Storonsky (born 1963), and 2 fines on EU group subsidiaries rather than Revolut Ltd (Bank of Lithuania EUR 3.5m AML fine, April 2025; Italian EUR 11.5m fine, April 2026). The UK banking business is moving to Revolut Bank UK Ltd (12871051), which needs its own screen.
